Those soldiers who, as you said, held that area. They were the security there, right? So if that was the case, I certainly didn't know that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's done now, but I didn't think the witness would know, so --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And indeed I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My words have been misinterpreted. I did not mention that this name whose name I mentioned is a witness, and especially that he had the status of a protected witness. So that the gentleman whom I was examining wouldn't know, would he? But in any case, it's all right. It's not so crucial that I would now ask that you adapt your ruling to my desires. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There will be redactions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you came from Mitrovica to Negoslavci, we've spoken about this to some extent, you say they are informing you that your company is at Ovcara, guarding a new group. My question is, were any of your officers then at Negoslavci when you received this information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I'm repeating myself. I don't believe I went to the command. I did probably though, but it's just that I don't remember who it was that I saw there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who could have ordered your company in your absence to do the security job at Ovcara on the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A commander has all the rights because he is the one issuing assignments and orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, just which commander are you talking?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is only one. Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic. Whether he did or didn't is not something that I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was there anyone else in addition to Vojnovic that could possibly have ordered the members of your company to go and do the security at Ovcara or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement to the OTP, it's page 10 in the English, paragraph 3, for the benefit of my learned friends. Page 10, paragraph 2, when you arrived at Ovcara, the JNA reservists withdrew to the yellow house. Which soldiers are we talking about here, since a while ago you said you had no idea where Joca Kafic and his soldiers had gone to. Who are these soldiers that we see here now going to the yellow house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only soldiers who would possibly have withdrawn to the yellow house were Joca Kafic's soldiers, although --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Although what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you think that I said this at the time and now I don't remember, well that's about it, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever go to the yellow house yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't go inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you go, if not inside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was outside the house. I passed the house several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was at that house, since you passed the house as you went about your duties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go into the house. I did say that, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Why did you notice the yellow house at all then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, there is a stretch of the road looking from Negoslavci in the direction of Sotin, so to the left there is a flat area, and that was the only house outside the forest, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can we please have that photograph displayed again, Exhibit 236, page 22. 256. Fine. Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we go. The hangars again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The yellow house, no need to mark anything. Where is it in this photograph? You have indicated the general direction, but there is a number of other buildings there. Was it near the buildings on the right-hand side of the photograph? My apologies. My apologies, we need photograph number 20 and zoom in a little. Could you please zoom in the left-hand side of the photograph? That's right. Sir, do you see the yellow house in this photograph? Could the technicians please bring back the first photograph, because -- well, yes. Okay. Right. Thank you very much. Excellent. Can you indicate the house now or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just please take a minute to get my bearings? This looks very much like the house, but I need to get my bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You will need a pen after that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can't see the hangars. If I could see the hangars maybe it would be easier, at least the road. I'm quite --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Let's bring back that first photograph, number 20, please. What about this angle? Can you see the yellow house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mark that as number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Why did you memorize this house of all houses, since we see that there are a lot of buildings in the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you understood me. Looking from Negoslavci in the direction of Sotin, this is the flat area, and to the left. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So that's your explanation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you had in the direction of the flat bit and then you notice something on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No need to tender this into evidence I believe it's sufficient for the Chamber to have heard the witness's explanation as to why he remembered this particular house. My next question: When you left for Ovcara did you have any radio equipment at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether Vojnovic had any telephone communications with the house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who came at Ovcara with you on the 20th of November? Was Jovica Trifunovic, a soldier, with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was myself, the driver, Trifunovic, Sapic, and perhaps some other soldiers who were off duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you all carry automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did all your military policemen within the hangar carry automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After securing the hangar on the 20th, did you secure some other facilities in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Such as?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We secured the hospital, the grammar school, the house full of explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also secure the safe of the payments institute at Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If you reread the statement you provided at the Belgrade Ovcara case, page 62. In the English that's page 61. On page 62 and for my learned friend from the Prosecution, that's page 61, you stated the following in your answer to the Presiding Judge you mentioned Kameni, and then you said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Borovic read slowly, please. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: "When we were securing the safe of the then payments institute," is that correct? That's what one can read in your statement at the Belgrade Ovcara case?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But that is different from what you have just told us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I can clarify. The safe wasn't being secured when there was money in it. When it was broken into and when the money was taken out, we were told to try and protect everything else that was inside the safe. Therefore, we didn't provide security per se, but I don't know what to call it. We were there on guard during the night, and I took part in one of the shifts as well. That's why we were -- I said we were not securing the safe, because it included only one night.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you were securing the safe during that one night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My learned friend Mr. Vasic asked you whether you know Aleksandar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is the general, then yes, I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the first time in Kragujevac, when he was introduced to me by Lieutenant-Colonel Jeftic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that he was born in Kragujevac as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that he had proceedings instituted before the military organs concerning the safe that was broken into?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Now, to go back to the issues relevant to the defence of my client. In the period defined here between 1730 and 2200 hours, were there any murders at the hangar at that time? I am asking you to be quite specific?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were there any killings in front of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: At that period were there any agricultural machines or machinery turned on in front of the hangar, tractors or some other type of machinery? And I have in mind the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the exception of the machinery at the back of the hangar, I -- we also gave it a thought for the soldiers to rest there, but in the front part where the entrance was, there were no machines there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And at that time when you were there and when your soldiers were there who had arrived there before you, did you see a loader right next to the entrance to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know for how long your soldiers had been securing prior to your arrival at 5.30 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to tell you that we have information according to which some people's -- some people claim that during the time wherein your soldiers were there and when you were there, that period being defined as of 4.30 p.m. onwards, that a tractor was on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was page 5.004, line 1 for the Chamber and the OTP. And on page 5.005, line 19, pertaining to the period as of 4.30 p.m., an hour after that some people stated that the military police withdrew from the hangar and Ovcara. So one hour later, perhaps that's around 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me then that such information is incorrect? You testified here that you went away at 2200 hours and that you were securing the prisoners throughout, as defined by you before. Irrespective of the exact time period, in case we don't agree on the exact time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't understood quite well. 4.30 or 5.00, what did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: As of the moment of the arrival of your soldiers, and during the time you were there, and up until 2200 hours when you left. Is this correct, or rather, the statement I quoted, is it incorrect, the statement is on page 5.005, stating that the military police withdrew from Ovcara as early as 5.00 p.m. Is that incorrect? The statement provides that there were no military policemen between 5.00 p.m. and 10.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at Ovcara at 5.00 p.m. As for the 2200 hours, well, it was dark. It could have been an hour and a half or up to two hours. I was there during that time. But whether that was between 5.00 and 7.00 p.m. or 10.00 p.m., I don't know. If I understood your question properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Since I can't put something that a particular witness stated here to you, I have to go the round about way, but I'll try to be more clear. There was a statement in possession of the Defence and the Chamber and the OTP know of it, by which the military police and its company were not there after 5.00 p.m. at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am to confirm that, it should be stated then that there were policemen after 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Up until when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I came there when it was already dark. I spent some time there. As to when exactly I came and left, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: To reiterate yet again?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But 5.00 is still ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If the operations diary states that the military police, in particular your company, and that is the operations diary of the 80th Kragujevac Brigade, that that company withdrew at 2200 hours, 2230. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: To go back to Aleksandar Vasiljevic, you spoke with him in 19 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Page 96, line 12, the witness's answer was "absolutely" and the transcript states "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, to my question I asked, then you stated that yes, the military police from the 80th Kragujevac Brigade was there between 5.00 p.m. and 10.30 p.m., and then I asked you if the operations log of the 80th Kragujevac Brigade states that the military police company withdrew from Ovcara at 10.30 p.m.; is that correct? What would be your answer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to answer yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree on the accuracy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when we left, but what you asked me is whether I agree with what is stated there, with the entry. If somebody wrote down that I withdrew at 10.30, that must be correct. I also agree with you that at 5.00 p.m. The military police was not withdrawn from Ovcara. I arrived later and we were there, therefore we agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe we've clarified the matter, Your Honours, and that I got the answer I was looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In the conversation you had with Milovan Jeftic and Aleksandar Vasiljevic, what were you asked to do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less everything I have explained so far concerning the Mitnica group, and the other group we called the hospital group. I briefed them on all of that, but in a much shorter form. We spent some time there, although I don't know how long, but we were in that restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting my learned friend, and it is my fault. I have been trying to follow the series of questions that arose at 96/13, and down to 97/1. And it said that the witness said absolutely. That was not our understanding of what was said. Secondly, the way the question was formulated was whether the entry was correct or whether in actual fact it reflected the actuality of what had occurred. And with the utmost respect to my learned friend, there is an element of confusion on that. Although the entry says 10.30, well that may well be. But the question surely is, does he agree that he left at 10.30, yes or no. I'd like the transcript, perhaps, to be listened to again, to see whether in actual fact he did use the word "absolutely", but it's left in a state of disarray, and obviously it's important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The effect of his last answer is apparent at the moment, Mr. Moore. I'm sure that it will be an interesting field for re-examination. I agree with you that until that last answer, everything you put was entirely justified. But I think the last answer has clarified the position. If there is confusion, re-examination is the answer. Carry on, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The witness clarified that on page 97. Perhaps we needn't listen to the tape. I'm absolutely certain that the witness said "absolutely." But perhaps we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were you asked to covertly tape the conversation you had with Joca Kafic? Were you asked to do that at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you propose to get a hold of the list that was in the possession of Joca Kafic containing the list of detainees on the 21st of November?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood your question, you are claiming that I knew that Joca Kafic was in possession of that document. I didn't. On the other hand, I offered my assistance to everyone in order to shed some lights as regards the Ovcara events, and I can claim at any time that I have been trying to shed some light concerning those events.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You came back from Sremska Mitrovica, you went to Negoslavci, and you heard that a part of your military police company was at Ovcara. After that you went and did everything you have explained today, and then withdrew. My question, hence, is the following: First your military policemen were there and then you were there securing the hangar. Throughout that time, did you go away from the hangar at any point before your withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of your question, you mentioned Mitrovica, but we are now talking about the 20th. If I understood the second part of your question, you stated, or you asked me whether, as of the moment I reunited with my unit, spent all of my time with them until we withdrew from Ovcara, then my answer is yes. But you have to bear in mind that I was going in and out of the hangar. But I was there with my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, to be specific, you were going in and out, there was a Pinzgauer with lights on in front of the hangar. My question, therefore, is, in front of the main entrance to the left there was a guard. Then the road. Across from the entrance, or across from the road was there a pit or a hole in the ground on the other side of the road? On that day did you see anyone taking people out and shooting those people at that time? Did you see any corpses or were there any such holes? And I mentioned the 20th of November, and that is not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any sort of a hole, I saw no corpses. No one was killed during the time I was at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Ovcara was within the 80th Kragujevac Brigade area of responsibility on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the 80th motorised.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you mention their area of responsibility? The 80th motorised was within OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I have in mind the area of responsibility of the 80th Kragujevac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In the morning on the 21st of November did anyone give you any kind of list of detained persons from the hangar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 21st or later I did not have any conversations with anyone, nobody asked me, and I didn't respond to any questions regarding the security of the group of prisoners from the hospital. This is on the 20th of November. I didn't discuss that with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You then left the hangar, and where did you go, the military police company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic that evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did members of your unit return that evening, once again to Ovcara in order to guard, to make it easier for you, the yellow house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not according to an order from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But do you know whether this happened without an order from you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a conversation with Novica Trifunovic, he said that he was given the assignment to secure the Sapic group [as interpreted], although I don't know who he got this assignment from and why they would be doing that anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that there are assertions that on the 21st of November, 1991, in the period that you were the person with the nickname Stuka, and were carrying out liquidations of people in the pit across from the hangar, how would you comment that assertion? This was in the period of the 20th of November when you were there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you said that I had the nickname Stuka.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No, not you. Did you hear of a person called Stuka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that that evening when you held the area around the hangar under control, there was no one by the name of Stuka there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that nobody with the nickname Stuka in this critical period of the 20th of November, could not have been carrying out any executions in front of the hangar entrance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood your question correctly once again, because I have the impression that the question constantly is -- could be taken in two ways. In the period that I was there, there was no liquidation, there was no abuse of prisoners, they were treated properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Have you heard of Jovan Dulovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am done with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that on page 100, line 20 there's something illogical. I think that the witness said something about an assignment to secure the yellow house, and here it says "Sapic's group."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can assist, Your Honour. The intervention is correct, but actually the text was the yellow house was secured with Sapic. That was the correct reply. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps the witness will help me by telling me what Sapic is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sapic is a military policeman, also who was on assignment at Ovcara. It's the name of a soldier. Because I was told, and I don't know this, but I was told that the two of them came back to guard the yellow house. Why and in compliance with whose command, I don't know. Whose order, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that answers Mr. Vasic's question. Now, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vezmarovic, I am Mr. Lukic, and I represent Mr. Sljivancanin. I'm going to be asking you questions. I think that you understood while looking at the screen that you need to make a little break before beginning your answer, so we need to have a good rhythm, so our questions and answers don't overlap, for the sake of the interprets. What I would like to do is to discuss some statutory things at the end of today's hearing and perhaps touch upon some topics that we will dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I would like to ask the usher to give this set of statements, and there are also exhibits there, so that you have them in front of you, so in the course of the examination you have all the copies in hard copy with you and there will also be some at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vezmarovic, you yourself said that you provided a number of statements to different organs and because we will be going through your statements and your testimony, I would like to ask you if you could look there, if you recall that the first time you practically gave a statement about the events in Ovcara was before the military tribunal and this was on the 8th of February, 1999. You perhaps don't remember the record of the date of the record, but was that not the first statement that you provided in the capacity of a witness, before the military court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can remember, it is true that I provided my first statement to the military tribunal in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Next in the sequence of events is your testimony in the case of the Belgrade-Ovcara case, this is the case against Miroljub Vujovic and others when you gave a statement to Judge Alimpic on the 24th of June, 2004.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, in the interim I also provided a statement to the Tribunal, and then the -- the new -- Novi Sad statement came.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct chronologically. Before that you provided a statement to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal which was given on the 13th and 18th of December, 2001; isn't that true? Yes, could you please confirm yes or no so it's recorded in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And finally, you appeared as a witness in the main hearing in the Ovcara case against Miroljub Vujovic et al on the 29th of October, 2004. This was before the special department of the military court -- of the district court in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to say something else and then I will ask you about that again. But let's finish these official public testimonies. Finally, you testified before the Belgrade courts in the Ovcara II case, as we call it, that was actually the case against Sasa Radak where you were heard again before the same Trial Chamber, this was in 2005, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I saw from your testimonies that you also provided a statement to the police during the sablja action. We did not have access to those statements even though we asked for them. When we use the word sablja, saber, could you please describe what that operation was, because we are going to be referring to it? Could you explain something about that period in Serbia and Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, simply speaking after of the assassination of Prime Minister Dzindzic there was an emergency state imposed in Serbia which lasted three months and during a certain period I was called to Belgrade to provide a statement, and that's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this was during the state of emergency in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can give me brief answers to the following questions, these are just some status things we're moving to the Vukovar events at that time you had the rank of reserve captain in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I read, and you said that here, and you also said that during the Belgrade trial, that you completed the school for reserve officers in Bileca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that Bileca is amongst the most elite schools for training infantry cadre at the time in the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that would apply even more broadly. I don't want to be modest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that there were special standards in order to admit persons to the Bileca school?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps this is in the record, when you were providing your particulars, but when did you attend this school in Bileca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in October 1977 that I went there, and I came back in 1978. For the first six months I was in Bileca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was also said after this training for reserve infantry officers, you were sent immediately after that for additional training to Pancevo for the military police, and this was part of your regular military term of duty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I also understood that after serving your term of duty in order to receive the assignment that you did receive in the Vukovar period, so in order to be able to be a company commander, you went through additional training and courses, I assume in Pancevo. Can you please tell us how many times this was in the period in relation to this period of 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Pancevo on two more occasions for additional trainings first for platoon commander and then I went for additional training for company commander of military police. The dates and the periods are something that I don't remember exactly, but this is something that you can see in my records or in my file. In any case, I went there twice before 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These training courses last for several months, and you have to pass examinations at the end; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when you received the rank of captain?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can check that in my military booklet. It's entered there exactly which date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And these general questions, we have heard that here, and I assume that you are going confirm that in view of the structure of the 80th Kragujevac Brigade, the military police company was a staff unit, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the Kragujevac, but the motorised brigade. And it was a staff unit, the company was an independent one. I don't know in what sense it would be a staff one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In view of the function of the police, the company's main assignment would be to secure the command units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It secures the commander in a location and during the movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The entire command also?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the entire command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I interrupt? Clear up something? On our numbering, page 107/1, but it's the commencement of an answer by the witness that says, "Not the Kragujevac but the motorised brigade." Could you please indicate, are you saying there that they are two distinct brigades or are you merely correcting the correct and indicating the correct description of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If I remember properly, what was said was the Kragujevac 80th Brigade, but in jargon it's either the Kragujevac brigade, but without the prefix "the 80th," so it's the 80th Motorised Brigade, but it's all one unit that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometimes I am using jargon here, but this actually affects my client the most because he really asks me to be very precise. So I apologise if I did not ask a question that was not exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I would like to ask the witness now is again to take his notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit 432. May we please place that on the ELMO? I don't know if it's on e-court, but in any case we can perhaps look at page 19 for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, you testified about the senior staff, or senior officers in your company, and what the composition was of the cadre that went to the Vukovar front. Am I understanding and seeing correctly that practically what is stated here on page 19 -- well, tell us, what are these names on page 19?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a list of a part of the military police company where we have Senad [as interpreted] Krstic, he's lieutenant second class, Pavlovic Mikan, he is a first class sergeant, and Radomir Stankovic, sergeant first class. I cannot remember for sure who was present at which point in time in Vukovar itself. The only thing that I know for sure is that Pavlovic Mikan was there because he was my company officer. Who of the others was there, who left, who had any problems, is really something I cannot remember anymore because some of these officers were in the other group that was taken away from me as early as Smederevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see under the number person that you mentioned is this Novica Trifunovic who is a private first class?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that person that the judge asked you about, Sapic, his name is Predrag but he is not on this list. He was just a military police officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Practically all the persons on this list up to number 22 do have some kind of rank, they're either officers or non-commissioned officers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am glad that I won't have to be looking at the clock all the time, and I will have enough time to continue with my cross-examination, but if we can now stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have extensive opportunities in the morning, Mr. Lukic. We will adjourn now and resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 10th day of May, 2006, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.30 p.m.,
